stick.name: Stick
stick.desc: A dry spruce branch about as long as your arm. Kindling, handles, shafts: the start of almost everything.

log.name: Spruce Log
log.desc: A 1.2 m length of spruce trunk, sticky with sap. Twelve kilos: carried on the shoulder, not in a pack.

stone.name: Stone
stone.desc: A fist-sized cobble of river granite, rounded by the glacier. Heavy, hard and endlessly useful.

flint.name: Flint
flint.desc: A glassy grey-black nodule of chert, the flint of these mountains. Knapped, it takes an edge sharper than steel.

fiber.name: Plant Fibre
fiber.desc: Tough strands stripped from dead fireweed stalks and sedge. Twist enough of it together and it holds.

bark.name: Birch Bark
bark.desc: Papery bark peeled from a paper birch. Its oils light even when damp; the inner bark makes cordage.

resin.name: Spruce Resin
resin.desc: Amber pitch scraped from wounded spruce. Burns hot and sooty, and sets like glue when it cools.

feather.name: Feather
feather.desc: A stiff grouse flight feather. Split and bound in threes, feathers steady an arrow's flight.

bone.name: Bone
bone.desc: A cleaned deer leg bone, dense and white. Carve it into needles and awls, or crack it for marrow.

sinew.name: Sinew
sinew.desc: Dried tendon pounded into fine threads. Stronger than any plant cord: it strings bows and sews hides.

hide_raw.name: Raw Hide
hide_raw.desc: A fresh deer hide, heavy and wet, still smelling of the animal. Scrape and smoke it before it rots.

hide_cured.name: Cured Hide
hide_cured.desc: Smoked buckskin with the hair left on, soft and supple. Turns the wind and sheds light snow.

wool.name: Goat Wool
wool.desc: Mountain goat underwool, combed from the brush where goats rub. Astonishingly warm for its weight.

cloth.name: Cloth
cloth.desc: Torn fabric: seat covers, a shirt, a curtain. Bandages, torch wicks, patches.

scrap_metal.name: Scrap Metal
scrap_metal.desc: Bent aluminium skin and steel brackets salvaged from wreckage. Cut, hammer and fold it into something useful.

wire.name: Wire
wire.desc: A tangle of copper and steel wire pulled from a control run. Lashings, snares, repairs.

duct_tape.name: Duct Tape
duct_tape.desc: Half a roll of silver duct tape. Fixes nearly anything, for a while.

rope.name: Rope
rope.desc: Three-strand rope twisted from plant fibre and bark. Lashings, shelter lines, hauling.

nails.name: Nails
nails.desc: Galvanised 3-inch framing nails, a little rusty. Worth their weight when you're building.

fuel_can.name: Jerrycan (Diesel)
fuel_can.desc: A 5-litre steel jerrycan of diesel for the station generator. It sloshes heavily with every step.

battery.name: Battery
battery.desc: A cold-rated lithium D-cell. Lanterns, radios and the scanner all run on these.

electronics.name: Electronic Parts
electronics.desc: Circuit boards, connectors and relays salvaged from instruments. Fragile; keep them dry.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: Black, light and brittle. Burns hotter and longer than wood, with almost no smoke.

tinder.name: Tinder Bundle
tinder.desc: A bird's nest of shredded birch bark, dry grass and lichen. It catches the weakest spark.

snow.name: Snow
snow.desc: A packed handful of clean snow. Melt it first: eating it cold costs precious body heat.

pine_needles.name: Spruce Needles
pine_needles.desc: A handful of green spruce needles. Steeped, they make a sharp, citrusy tea rich in vitamin C.

usnea.name: Old Man's Beard
usnea.desc: Pale green Usnea lichen hanging from spruce limbs. Naturally antiseptic, and superb tinder.

tin_can.name: Empty Tin
tin_can.desc: A rinsed-out food tin. Punch two holes and add a wire bail, and it becomes a billy can.

lamp_oil.name: Lamp Oil
lamp_oil.desc: A litre of kerosene in a dented tin bottle. Fuel for the hurricane lantern; a splash lights a stubborn fire.

wool_blanket.name: Wool Blanket
wool_blanket.desc: A heavy striped trade blanket from the ranger cabin. Cut and belted, it makes a fine winter coat.

emergency_blanket.name: Emergency Blanket
emergency_blanket.desc: A crinkling Mylar space blanket from the crash kit. Reflects your own body heat back at you.

coffee_grounds.name: Instant Coffee
coffee_grounds.desc: A foil sachet of instant coffee from someone's flight bag. Add boiling water.

o2_bottle_empty.name: Empty Oxygen Cylinder
o2_bottle_empty.desc: An aluminium oxygen cylinder, gauge on zero. The station's concentrator can refill it.

berries.name: Huckleberries
berries.desc: Dark, tart huckleberries, the last of the season, wrinkled by frost. A mouthful of sugar.

mushroom.name: Hedgehog Mushroom
mushroom.desc: A pale hedgehog mushroom with soft teeth instead of gills. One of the few that are hard to mistake.

meat_raw.name: Raw Venison
meat_raw.desc: A dark red cut of deer meat. Cook it through: raw game carries parasites.

meat_cooked.name: Cooked Venison
meat_cooked.desc: Seared over open flame, smoky and lean. Real fuel for a cold body.

meat_dried.name: Venison Jerky
meat_dried.desc: Thin strips of venison smoked hard over a slow fire. Light, salty, and keeps for weeks.

fish_raw.name: Raw Trout
fish_raw.desc: A bull trout from Loon Lake, cold and slick. Gut it and cook it.

fish_cooked.name: Cooked Trout
fish_cooked.desc: Flaky, pink and rich with fat. The best thing you have eaten in days.

ration_bar.name: Emergency Ration
ration_bar.desc: A 400-kilocalorie survival bar that tastes of lemon and sawdust. Five-year shelf life.

canned_beans.name: Canned Beans
canned_beans.desc: A dented tin of beans in tomato sauce. Better warmed by the fire, but fine cold.

pine_tea.name: Spruce Needle Tea
pine_tea.desc: Hot, resinous and faintly lemony. Warms your hands first, then your core.

coffee.name: Hot Coffee
coffee.desc: Bitter instant coffee, scalding hot. Warms you up and pushes back the fatigue for a while.

water_unsafe.name: Untreated Water
water_unsafe.desc: Clear glacial creek water in a bottle. Probably fine. Giardia says otherwise.

water_boiled.name: Boiled Water
water_boiled.desc: Water brought to a rolling boil and left to cool. Safe to drink, faintly smoky.

bottle_empty.name: Empty Bottle
bottle_empty.desc: A 750 ml plastic bottle. Pack it with snow or fill it at a creek, then boil.

stone_axe.name: Stone Axe
stone_axe.desc: A knapped stone head lashed into a split spruce haft. Crude and heavy, and it will fell a tree, slowly.

hatchet.name: Hatchet
hatchet.desc: A forged-steel hatchet from the Otter's survival kit. Short, sharp and well balanced.

felling_axe.name: Felling Axe
felling_axe.desc: A long-handled 3½-pound felling axe from the Ashford Mine store. Drops a spruce in a dozen swings.

knife.name: Bushcraft Knife
knife.desc: A full-tang carbon-steel knife. It skins, carves and cuts cord, and it never leaves your belt.

stone_knife.name: Chert Blade
stone_knife.desc: A razor flake of chert hafted in a wrapped stick. Brittle, but sharp enough to skin and carve.

spear.name: Hunting Spear
spear.desc: A two-metre spruce shaft tipped with knapped chert. Keeps a wolf at arm's length or pins a trout.

bow.name: Hunting Bow
bow.desc: A flat-limbed bow with a 45-pound draw. Silent, and deadly within thirty metres.

arrow.name: Arrow
arrow.desc: Straight shaft, stone point, three split feathers. Recover them: they are hard to make.

torch.name: Torch
torch.desc: A cloth-wrapped branch soaked in spruce pitch. Light, a little heat, and a way to keep wolves honest.

flare.name: Road Flare
flare.desc: A red magnesium flare: fifteen minutes of blinding light and choking smoke. Nothing with fur comes near.

flare_gun.name: Flare Gun
flare_gun.desc: An orange 12-gauge signal pistol from the Otter's survival kit. Not a weapon, but bears don't know that.

flare_shell.name: Flare Cartridge
flare_shell.desc: A 12-gauge red-star signal cartridge. Climbs 150 metres and burns for seven seconds.

lantern.name: Hurricane Lantern
lantern.desc: A galvanised kerosene lantern. Steady, windproof light for six hours on a fill of lamp oil.

ice_axe.name: Ice Axe
ice_axe.desc: Owen Burke's mountaineering axe: steel pick, adze and spike. Cuts steps, anchors you, arrests falls.

canteen.name: Canteen
canteen.desc: A one-litre stainless canteen. Unlike a plastic bottle, you can set it straight in the coals.

cooking_pot.name: Cooking Pot
cooking_pot.desc: A blackened billy can with a wire bail. Melt snow, boil water, brew tea.

binoculars.name: Binoculars
binoculars.desc: 8×42 roof-prism binoculars, fogged at the edges. Scout the route before you commit to it.

survey_scanner.name: Survey Scanner
survey_scanner.desc: A ruggedised field scanner meant for Kestrel Station, its screen cracked in the crash. Hold it on something to learn how it's made.

map.name: Topographic Map
map.desc: A 1:50,000 sheet of the Aldous Range, soft from folding. Loon Lake is circled in pencil.

compass.name: Compass
compass.desc: A liquid-filled baseplate compass. The needle still finds north in a whiteout.

hammer.name: Claw Hammer
hammer.desc: A steel claw hammer with a fibreglass handle. Drives nails, pulls them, builds things that last.

lighter.name: Lighter
lighter.desc: A cheap butane lighter, half full. A hundred lights, maybe, if your fingers are warm enough.

matches.name: Matches
matches.desc: Strike-anywhere matches in a waxed box. Each one counts.

ferro_rod.name: Ferro Rod
ferro_rod.desc: A ferrocerium rod and steel striker. Thousands of fat orange sparks, if you have good tinder.

bow_drill.name: Bow Drill
bow_drill.desc: Spindle, hearth board and a cord-strung bow. Hard work, but it makes fire from nothing.

bone_needle.name: Bone Needle
bone_needle.desc: Carved from a deer's cannon bone and polished on stone. With sinew, you can sew hide.

o2_bottle.name: Oxygen Cylinder
o2_bottle.desc: A 2-litre aluminium cylinder of medical oxygen at 200 bar. About forty-five minutes on a mask.

crampons.name: Crampons
crampons.desc: Twelve-point steel crampons that strap over stiff boots. Without them the icefall is a death slide.

climbing_rope.name: Climbing Rope
climbing_rope.desc: Forty metres of 9.8 mm dynamic rope, still coiled the way a guide coils it.

o2_mask.name: Oxygen Mask
o2_mask.desc: A silicone mask with a reservoir bag and flow regulator. Clip a cylinder to it and breathe.

goggles.name: Glacier Goggles
goggles.desc: Mirrored goggles with side shields. They cut glare and whiteout and keep your eyes from freezing shut.

slit_goggles.name: Slit Goggles
slit_goggles.desc: Snow goggles carved from bone, with narrow slits. Crude, but they stop snow blindness.

bandage.name: Bandage
bandage.desc: A roll of clean cloth. Stops bleeding, if you are quick about it.

first_aid_kit.name: First Aid Kit
first_aid_kit.desc: An aviation first aid kit: dressings, antiseptic, tape, gloves. Enough to put you back together once.

painkillers.name: Painkillers
painkillers.desc: Ibuprofen, 200 mg. Dulls a sprain and takes the edge off frostbite pain.

splint.name: Splint
splint.desc: Two straight sticks padded with cloth and lashed tight. Immobilises a sprain so you can keep walking.

herbal_poultice.name: Lichen Poultice
herbal_poultice.desc: Usnea lichen packed in cloth. Mildly antiseptic; wounds heal clean and a little faster.

wool_hat.name: Wool Toque
wool_hat.desc: A thick hand-knit toque. You lose more heat through a bare head than you would believe.

fur_hat.name: Fur Hat
fur_hat.desc: A hide cap lined with fur, earflaps tied under the chin.

field_jacket.name: Softshell Jacket
field_jacket.desc: A technician's softshell. Fine for a floatplane hop; hopeless for a night on a glacier.

wool_sweater.name: Wool Sweater
wool_sweater.desc: A heavy cable-knit sweater that still smells of the ranger's pipe. Warm even when damp.

hide_coat.name: Hide Coat
hide_coat.desc: A knee-length coat of smoked hide, fur turned inward. Heavy, windproof, and it creaks when you move.

blanket_capote.name: Blanket Capote
blanket_capote.desc: A hooded coat cut from a striped wool trade blanket, belted with rope. A centuries-old winter design.

parka.name: Expedition Parka
parka.desc: A down parka with a fur-ruffed tunnel hood. The warmest thing you own, until the station.

down_suit.name: Down Suit
down_suit.desc: A one-piece eight-thousander down suit from the station stores. Only the summit asks for this much.

hiking_pants.name: Hiking Trousers
hiking_pants.desc: Quick-dry nylon trousers. Light, and about as warm as a wet newspaper.

hide_leggings.name: Hide Leggings
hide_leggings.desc: Fur-lined hide leggings tied at the knee and ankle. Warm, windproof, and noisy in the brush.

insulated_pants.name: Insulated Overtrousers
insulated_pants.desc: Synthetic-fill overtrousers with full side zips. The wind stops at the fabric.

work_gloves.name: Work Gloves
work_gloves.desc: Split-leather work gloves. They save your hands from splinters and the worst of the cold.

fur_mitts.name: Fur Mitts
fur_mitts.desc: Gauntlet mitts of fur-lined hide on a cord around the neck. Clumsy, and wonderfully warm.

boots.name: Hiking Boots
boots.desc: Waterproof leather hiking boots, broken in. Too soft for crampons.

mountaineering_boots.name: Mountaineering Boots
mountaineering_boots.desc: Stiff double boots with insulated liners and a welt for step-in crampons.

backpack_torn.name: Torn Backpack
backpack_torn.desc: A 40-litre pack with a ripped lid and one frayed strap. It still carries.

backpack.name: Hiking Backpack
backpack.desc: Your old pack, restitched with sinew and patched with hide. Rides well, holds more.

expedition_pack.name: Expedition Pack
expedition_pack.desc: A 75-litre expedition pack with a stiff frame and ice tool loops. Built for the summit.

survival_manual.name: Survival Manual
survival_manual.desc: A water-stained wilderness survival handbook from the Otter's seat pocket. Fire, shelter, water, first aid.

radio_handheld.name: Handheld Radio
radio_handheld.desc: A two-way VHF radio from the ranger cabin, with a spare battery. The speaker still hisses.

transceiver_module.name: Transceiver Module
transceiver_module.desc: A sealed Ku-band transceiver in a foam-lined case. The relay's heart, if it survived shipping.

battery_pack.name: Relay Battery Pack
battery_pack.desc: A 24-volt lithium pack for the summit relay. Heavy, cold-rated, fully charged.

mine_key.name: Depot Key
mine_key.desc: A brass padlock key on a loop of orange cord, tagged 'O.B. — ADIT DEPOT'.

station_keycard.name: Station Keycard
station_keycard.desc: A Kestrel Station access card: 'Dr. E. Hale — All Areas'.

dale_logbook.name: Pilot's Logbook
dale_logbook.desc: Dale Morrow's flight log. The last entry is shaky: 'Carb heat on. Still losing power.'
